text:
Aditya Rao: @channel FYI: we’re rolling out **Quality Guardrails Gating** for **Optimize “apply”** (batching/caching/quantization/routing tweaks). This is to prevent the “Optimize saved $$ but quality dipped” class of incidents.

What’s changing (esp. if you use internal Optimize tooling / scripts):
• Optimize apply will now run an eval suite (prompt set + metrics + thresholds) before config changes can be applied.
• You’ll see a gating outcome: `PASS` / `FAIL` / `TIMEOUT` (+ metric deltas + links to artifacts).
• Rollout is staged via feature flags: **observe-only → soft-block (override possible) → hard-block**.
• Gating is enforced in the control plane (so Console + API + internal callers are all covered).

Timeline (current plan):
• This week: observe-only in staging + internal dogfood tenants
• Next 2–3 weeks: soft-block for a small internal slice + design partners
• Following: GA ramp to hard-block for Optimize applies (with audited override for restricted roles)

Action for teams using internal Optimize:
1) If your workload doesn’t have a prompt set / tags yet, please ping #eng-ml (Jonas/Selene) so we can map you to an existing suite or add coverage.
2) If you have a CI job that auto-applies recommendations: please be ready for `FAIL/TIMEOUT` responses and handle them (no silent retries that hammer the runner).
3) If you need an override pathway for oncall / customer escalations, see below (Naomi/Ethan are tracking RBAC + auditing requirements).

Links:
• PRD: https://redwood-internal/confluence/x/optimize-guardrails-prd
• Tech overview: https://redwood-internal/confluence/x/optimize-guardrails-service
• Runbook (draft): https://redwood-internal/confluence/x/optimize-guardrails-runbook

Office hours: Thu 1–2pm PT (invite going out). Drop questions here.

Priya Natarajan: +1. we’ve had a few too many “cost win → quality regression” loops. this is a platform-wide reliability investment. thanks everyone for helping with prompt coverage + rollout discipline.

Dylan Brooks: does this mean Console apply will start showing a new modal/panel? (we have internal users who apply from the Optimize page a lot)

Aditya Rao: yep. Console will show a gating results panel (pass/fail/timeout) with the key metrics and a link to the eval run summary. in observe-only it’ll be informational; in soft/hard block it’ll gate the “Apply” action.

Ethan Park: adding detail: enforcement is at the **Optimize apply endpoint** in the control plane. so:
• internal CLI calling apply → gets the same decision payload
• Console calls → same
• any direct writes to config will be blocked if they go through the supported API paths (and audited)

Jonas Weber: for folks asking “do we need to hand-author evals?” — no, not to start. we have baseline suites by workload type (chat/tool-calling/structured output) + model family. BUT we do need prompt set tags to select the right suite.

If you can share even a small redacted prompt set (10–30 prompts) that represent your workload, it helps reduce false passes/false blocks. DM me or post in #eng-ml.

Sofia Ivanova: question from runtime side: are we isolating eval traffic? worried about dogfood turning into extra load on shared clusters during peak.

Sean Gallagher: yep. eval runner uses a separate queue + concurrency limits. also we’re starting with observe-only specifically to measure backlog/latency before we block anything. if you’re planning bulk “apply simulation” runs, please coordinate w/ #eng-sre so we can schedule off-peak.

Naomi Feldman: on overrides: what’s the expected policy? (who can override, do we require justification + 2nd approver, etc)

Ethan Park: current draft policy:
• soft-block stage: override is available for restricted roles only (eng-oncall / designated customer success engineers) with **required justification**
• overrides are fully audited (who/what/why + which eval suite + results)
• we’re still deciding if “2-person approval” is required for enterprise tier applies; will follow up once leadership signs off

Owen Phillips: from support POV: pls make sure the failure payload is something we can paste into a ticket w/o needing an engineer to interpret. “rubric_score -0.07 (CI) < threshold” is fine; “metric_12 failed” is not :)

Aditya Rao: 100%. one of the explicit pilot success criteria is “support can explain outcome from UI + audit event without eng help.” we’ll keep iterating on the failure reasons.

Connor O'Brien: release train question: when does this hit prod for internal tenants? trying to plan around a couple perf experiments that call Optimize apply.

Sean Gallagher: no hard date yet, but we’ll post in #eng-releases before any prod flag ramp. for internal tenants: earliest soft-block ramp would be mid next week, but only for a small slice.

Elliot Price: docs note: we’re drafting internal + external wording for “blocked due to quality checks” vs “service issue/timeout.” if you have strong opinions on tone (esp. customer-facing), please comment on the outline: https://redwood-internal/confluence/x/optimize-guardrails-docs

Aditya Rao: keep questions coming. also if you have an internal automation that currently “auto-apply on schedule,” please reply here w/ the repo/name so we can make sure you’re not surprised when soft-block flips on.
